evidence.title: Lebenslauf Olaf Scholz
evidence.claim: Olaf Scholz was elected in December 2021 as the ninth Federal Chancellor of Germany and led the first traffic-light coalition at federal level.
evidence.locator: Biography section near the opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official federal biography page with a stable office chronology.
evidence.period_fit: Establishes Scholz's office and inherited baseline for 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Scholz; this is his official office record.
contrary_evidence: None on office status.

evidence.title: Grundgesetz
evidence.claim: Article 63 says the Chancellor is elected by the Bundestag on the Federal President's proposal, and Article 65 says the Chancellor sets policy guidelines while ministers lead their departments independently; Article 65a gives the Defence Minister command authority in the defense portfolio.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text from the Bundestag site, stable and authoritative.
evidence.period_fit: Directly applicable in 2022 and defines Scholz's authority and constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional constraint on Scholz's office, not personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: Ministerial autonomy and coalition politics materially limit direct chancellor control.

evidence.title: Policy statement by Olaf Scholz, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany and Member of the German Bundestag, 27 February 2022 in Berlin
evidence.claim: Scholz said that with regard to nuclear sharing Germany would procure a modern replacement for the outdated Tornado jets in good time, and that the F-35 could be used as a carrier aircraft.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous statement by the Chancellor on the official federal website.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 decision point on Germany's nuclear-sharing posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz statement and policy choice; cabinet-level commitment under his leadership.
contrary_evidence: This preserved rather than reduced Germany's nuclear-sharing role.
Critics later argued it locked Germany into nuclear deterrence for years.

evidence.title: Policy statement by Olaf Scholz, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany and Member of the German Bundestag, 27 February 2022 in Berlin
evidence.claim: Scholz said the government would strengthen resilience against cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns and against attacks on critical infrastructure and communication channels.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous statement by the Chancellor on the official federal website.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 statement on a dual-use/catastrophic-risk adjacent domain.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz policy framing; cabinet-level priority under his leadership.
contrary_evidence: This is resilience rhetoric, not a demonstrated institutional reform or published cyber-risk doctrine.
It is indirect for nuclear/existential-risk scoring.

evidence.title: The Federal Foreign Office on yesterday’s statement by the five permanent members of the UN Security Council
evidence.claim: The German Government welcomed the P5 statement that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and said dialogue and cooperation among the five states were more important than ever for reducing tensions and escalation risk.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official foreign ministry statement issued the day after the P5 declaration.
evidence.period_fit: Very close to the 2022 period and directly relevant to nuclear rhetoric and de-escalation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level position under Scholz's cabinet; not a private Scholz-only remark.
contrary_evidence: It is a general government statement, not a personal command decision.
No direct implementation mechanism is specified.

evidence.title: First Meeting of States Parties to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
evidence.claim: Germany participated as an observer in the first TPNW meeting, saying the government remains committed to a world without nuclear weapons, sees the NPT as the central framework, and is not joining the TPNW because of NATO responsibilities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official German foreign ministry explanation of the government's nuclear-disarmament posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level attribution under Scholz; the decision reflects government posture, not a personal order from a nuclear commander.
contrary_evidence: The same text says NATO responsibilities keep Germany outside the TPNW.
The observer status is symbolic and does not itself reduce risk.

evidence.title: Non-Proliferation and Disarmament Initiative - 11th High-level Meeting Joint High-level Statement
evidence.claim: Germany and NPDI partners reaffirmed support for the NPT's full implementation, the ultimate goal of a world without nuclear weapons, and practical nuclear risk-reduction and disarmament steps.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official multilateral statement naming Germany as a member state and setting out specific nonproliferation aims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution, not Scholz personally, but under his chancellorship.
contrary_evidence: The statement is multilateral and not specific to Scholz's personal initiative.
It reflects aspiration more than proved outcome.

evidence.title: Statement of the G7 Non-Proliferation Directors Group on a Nuclear Safety and Security Framework for Ukraine
evidence.claim: The G7 called for urgent measures to protect nuclear installations in Ukraine, emphasizing physical integrity, functional safety systems, secure power supply, staff able to make decisions free of undue pressure, and reliable communications with regulators.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official G7 nonproliferation statement tied to the Ukraine war and nuclear safety conditions.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 crisis period and directly relevant to nuclear accident prevention.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level German participation under Scholz's chancellorship; not a singular Scholz-only initiative.
contrary_evidence: This concerns Ukraine's nuclear plants, not Germany's own command-and-control.
It is crisis mitigation, not a structural treaty breakthrough.

evidence.title: Speech by Olaf Scholz at the 77th general debate of the United Nations General Assembly
evidence.claim: Scholz described Russia as a major nuclear power using violence to shift borders, condemned the war against Ukraine, and said Germany would support Ukraine with weapons and sanctions while standing by the UN order.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Scholz speech on the federal government's official archive page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz rhetoric and policy signaling; the support commitments reflect his government.
contrary_evidence: This is general crisis diplomacy, not a direct nuclear safety or arms-control decision.
It accepts armed support to Ukraine, which can be read as escalatory in a broader security sense.

evidence.title: Germany to Buy up to 35 Lockheed F-35 Fighter Jets - Sources
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Germany would purchase 35 F-35 fighters to replace the aging Tornado aircraft in the nuclear-sharing role, with the Tornado being the only German jet able to carry U.S. nuclear bombs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting is strong independent contemporaneous coverage, even though the accessible host is VOA.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indicates the government decision taken under Scholz's leadership; not a personal nuclear order.
contrary_evidence: This is a continuation of nuclear-sharing capability rather than risk reduction.
The story notes France and procurement tradeoffs, showing broader strategic rather than safety logic.

evidence.title: F-35: Why Germany is opting for the US stealth bomber
evidence.claim: DW reported that only the opposition Left Party clearly rejected the F-35 purchase, warning that nuclear sharing would fuel the danger of nuclear war in Europe, while an ECFR expert said the F-35 was better suited than older aircraft for delivering a nuclear weapon.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with both expert explanation and documented domestic criticism.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 debate around the procurement choice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Scholz's cabinet decision; the criticism targets the government choice rather than a separate actor.
contrary_evidence: This is an analysis piece, not a primary decision record.
It contains a pro-F-35 expert view as well as anti-nuclear-sharing criticism.

reasons.reason: Secondary analysis with mixed expert views; treat as corroborative context for the F-35 debate, not core proof of Scholz-specific existential-risk judgment.

evidence.title: Linke fragt Beschaffung des Kampfflugzeuges F-35
evidence.claim: The Left parliamentary group asked whether buying the F-35 would commit Germany to nuclear sharing for decades and noted earlier government concerns about technical risks and a poorer cost-benefit ratio.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary parliamentary record of contemporaneous criticism and the government's earlier risk concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material to Scholz's government decision; it captures legislative scrutiny of the cabinet's choice.
contrary_evidence: This is opposition framing, not an executive defense or neutral technical assessment.
It does not prove the final operational impact of the purchase.

reasons.reason: Opposition scrutiny of the procurement choice is accountability context, not independent evidence of the ruler's conduct.

evidence.title: Jahresabrüstungsbericht 2022
evidence.claim: The German government summarized 2022 as a year in which it took responsibility for arms control, disarmament, and nonproliferation under difficult conditions, including proposals for risk reduction and disarmament verification, observer participation at the TPNW meeting, and G7 work on Ukrainian nuclear safety.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official retrospective government summary of 2022 actions; useful corroboration but not contemporaneous.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective summary of 2022 policy rather than direct contemporaneous evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level attribution under Scholz; indirect but relevant to end-of-year posture.
contrary_evidence: Published in 2023, so it is retrospective and may smooth over internal disagreement.
It summarizes government action rather than Scholz's personal decisions.

reasons.reason: Retrospective government summary should corroborate the 2022 record, not carry decisive weight on its own.

evidence.title: Televised address by Federal Chancellor Olaf Scholz on the Russian attack against Ukraine
evidence.claim: Scholz described Russia's attack on Ukraine as unjustified aggression, said Germany had pursued diplomacy before the invasion, and announced sanctions while insisting the conflict must not spread.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous statement by the Chancellor on the official federal website.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz statement and federal policy position.
contrary_evidence: The speech pairs condemnation with sanctions and deterrence rather than immediate negotiated settlement.
It is a public justification, not proof that all alternatives were exhausted.

evidence.title: In policy shift, Berlin to deliver defensive weapons to Ukraine
evidence.claim: Germany shifted policy to supply Ukraine with defensive anti-tank weapons, Stinger missiles, and ammunition, with Scholz calling Russia's invasion a turning point and saying Ukraine should be able to defend itself.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting with direct contemporaneous attribution and clear policy details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level decision under Scholz; the quote is directly attributed to him.
contrary_evidence: It marks a break from prior restraint on arms exports to war zones.
It supports defense, but also widens Germany's military involvement in the war.

evidence.title: Federal Government commits to additional aid
evidence.claim: At a donors' conference, Scholz pledged an additional 125 million euros for humanitarian aid and said the funds were also intended to increase Ukraine's ability to defend itself against Russian aggression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government summary with direct attribution to the Chancellor and conference context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz pledge, under federal executive authority.
contrary_evidence: Humanitarian aid is peace-supportive, but the same package also reinforces wartime defense.
It does not by itself show a negotiated peace strategy.

evidence.title: Germany's Scholz pushes for Ukraine ceasefire in call with Putin
evidence.claim: Scholz urged Putin to agree to a ceasefire as soon as possible, saying a truce was needed to improve the humanitarian situation and allow progress toward a diplomatic solution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting on a direct government-spokesperson account of the call.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz's call with Putin through the government spokesperson.
contrary_evidence: This is a ceasefire push, not a verified breakthrough.
The report does not show Russian acceptance or concrete de-escalation results.

evidence.title: Human Rights Commissioner Luise Amtsberg on today’s publication of the report produced under the OSCE’s Moscow Mechanism documenting violations of international law and human rights in Ukraine
evidence.claim: Germany said the OSCE Moscow Mechanism report documented severe breaches of international humanitarian law and human rights, possible war crimes, and targeted killings and abductions of civilians, and that Germany would help ensure accountability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official foreign-office statement summarizing an independent expert report and Germany's response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Scholz's chancellorship.
contrary_evidence: This is support for investigations, not direct command over battlefield conduct.
It relies on an OSCE expert report rather than a German operational record.

evidence.title: Joint statement on Ukraine’s application against Russia at the International Court of Justice
evidence.claim: Germany joined a statement welcoming Ukraine's ICJ case, saying Russia had no lawful basis for military action, urging compliance with the ICJ's order to suspend military operations, and endorsing accountability and peaceful settlement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary diplomatic/legal statement with Germany named among the signatories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Scholz; not a private or military act.
contrary_evidence: The statement supports lawfare and accountability, not a direct ceasefire.
It is multilateral and not unique to Scholz's personal initiative.

evidence.title: Sanctions will not be lifted until Russia signs peace deal with Ukraine - Germany's Scholz
evidence.claim: Scholz said sanctions imposed after the invasion would stay until Russia reaches a peace agreement with Ukraine and Germany would not accept Russia's annexation of Crimea.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting with direct attribution and clear date-specific policy content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Scholz as head of government.
contrary_evidence: The policy preserves pressure rather than quick compromise.
It rejects territorial revision, but does not itself produce peace talks.

evidence.title: Putin will not dictate Ukraine peace terms: Scholz
evidence.claim: Scholz said Russia would not win the war, rejected a dictated peace, and insisted that Ukraine, not Russia, must decide the terms of any agreement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting from a public Scholz speech with direct quotations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz public position.
contrary_evidence: It rejects coercive settlement, but also commits to continued Western support.
It does not show a negotiated result or a ceasefire gain.

evidence.title: Germany to send Ukraine arms for as long as needed - Scholz
evidence.claim: Scholz said Germany would continue sending weapons to Ukraine for as long as Ukraine needed support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting of a direct public statement by the Chancellor.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz statement.
contrary_evidence: This can be read as prolonging military support rather than pushing a quick settlement.
The report itself gives no endpoint or peace framework.

evidence.title: Ukraine security guarantees will not be same as for NATO member - Scholz
evidence.claim: Scholz said Germany and its allies were discussing security guarantees for Ukraine after the war, but they would not be the same as NATO membership guarantees.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report of a direct broadcast interview with the Chancellor.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz statement about allied policy.
contrary_evidence: The guarantees are prospective and undefined.
The statement is cautious and does not commit Germany to a concrete settlement architecture.

evidence.title: Speech by Olaf Scholz, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany and Member of the German Bundestag, at the 77th general debate of the United Nations General Assembly
evidence.claim: Scholz said Russia's war of occupation against Ukraine had no justification, rejected a dictated peace, and framed continued support for Ukraine with weapons, sanctions, and diplomacy as necessary to uphold the UN order.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous Scholz speech in the official federal archive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz rhetoric and government policy signaling.
contrary_evidence: The speech supports arming Ukraine, which is not pure de-escalation.
It relies on broad political framing rather than a concrete peace agreement.

evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz bei der Konferenz zum Wiederaufbau der Ukraine am 25. Oktober 2022 in Berlin
evidence.claim: Scholz called for a peaceful, prosperous, and resilient Ukraine, said Germany and partners would keep supporting Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, and military means, and presented reconstruction as a long-term international task.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Scholz speech in the official bulletin archive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz statement and hosting role.
contrary_evidence: The speech treats military aid and reconstruction as parallel, not separate, tracks.
It is forward-looking and does not prove conflict termination.

evidence.title: Deutschland 2022
evidence.claim: Amnesty said unzureichende Ermittlungen bei Vorwürfen über diskriminierende Personenkontrollen and the lack of an independent complaint mechanism continued to block justice for police abuse complaints in Germany.
evidence.locator: Berichtszeitraum 1. Januar 2022 bis 31. Dezember 2022; section on 'Recht auf Gerechtigkeit, Wahrheit und Wiedergutmachung'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights-organization country report covering the full target year; specific findings are explicit and well-sourced.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 and names the relevant police-accountability gap.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect ruler attribution only; this is a national institutional condition under Scholz's government, not a personal order.
contrary_evidence: Germany remained an open reporting environment rather than a closed repressive system.
The report criticizes investigation quality, not a pattern of systematic state terror.

evidence.title: Deutschland 2022
evidence.claim: Amnesty said some protests were disproportionately restricted and that a court held permanent protest camps protected by the freedom of assembly.
evidence.locator: Berichtszeitraum 1. Januar 2022 bis 31. Dezember 2022; section on 'Recht auf Versammlungsfreiheit'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same annual report, but this is a distinct claim on protest rights and restrictions with direct 2022 relevance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution to the federal political environment under Scholz; protest control was mostly exercised by Länder and local authorities.
contrary_evidence: The same report also notes a court-protected protest-camp precedent, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly repressive.
The restrictions discussed are not evidence of nationwide political terror.

evidence.title: Deutschland 2022
evidence.claim: Amnesty reported that in August 2022 a 16-year-old Senegalese refugee was killed by several shots from a machine gun during a disproportionate police operation, with criminal investigations still ongoing at year-end.
evidence.locator: Berichtszeitraum 1. Januar 2022 bis 31. Dezember 2022; section on discrimination / police action
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific, contemporaneous, and materially important incident documented by a leading rights NGO.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Weak-to-indirect national attribution: a police killing under a Scholz-era government, but operational control was regional and incident-specific.
contrary_evidence: The report describes an isolated severe incident, not a generalized national terror policy.
Investigations were still ongoing, so final legal responsibility was unsettled at year-end.

evidence.title: BASU c. ALLEMAGNE
evidence.claim: The Court held that Germany failed to secure an effective independent investigation into an arguable racial-profiling complaint arising from a police identity check, violating Article 14 in conjunction with Article 8.
evidence.locator: Judgment summary, introduction and key holding
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative judicial finding from the ECHR on a German policing and discrimination case.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 judgment, directly relevant to the year's accountability environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional attribution, not personal; it reflects state-level investigative failure under Scholz's chancellorship.
contrary_evidence: The case concerns a 2012 stop and the adequacy of later review, not a 2022 order by Scholz.
It shows a remedy failure more than direct policy abuse.

evidence.title: Versammlungsrechtlicher Schutz eines Protestcamps und seiner infrastrukturellen Einrichtungen
evidence.claim: The Federal Administrative Court held that a protest camp can generally count as a protected assembly under Article 8 GG and that its necessary infrastructure can also fall under assembly protection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Binding domestic court decision on protest rights and their protection scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indicates the legal environment under Scholz's government, not a personal directive by Scholz.
contrary_evidence: The case also confirms that authorities may still limit duration in some circumstances.
This is a legal-protection source, not evidence of executive restraint by itself.

evidence.title: Bundeskabinett - Ergebnisse
evidence.claim: The cabinet adopted a draft law to strengthen measures for democratic participation, diversity, extremism prevention, and political education.
evidence.locator: TOP-1-Liste / agenda items for the 44th cabinet meeting on 14 December 2022
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official cabinet decision published on the federal government site, contemporaneous with the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level action under Scholz; precise implementation and downstream effect remain broader than Scholz alone.
contrary_evidence: This is a draft-law decision, not proof of immediate harm reduction.
The measure is preventive and institutional, so its effect is indirect.

evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz zu 25 Jahren Freundeskreis Yad Vashem in Deutschland
evidence.claim: Scholz said the Nazis had begun their murderous intent by trying to erase Jewish life and used the speech to reaffirm Germany's historical responsibility toward Jewish life and remembrance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Scholz speech in the federal bulletin archive.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 speech, useful for public stance and vulnerable-group protection context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz rhetoric; it is a public statement, not an operational security order.
contrary_evidence: Rhetoric is not the same as enforcement or complaint-handling reform.
The speech is symbolic and commemorative, not a concrete anti-violence program.

evidence.title: Couverture de base pour les réfugiés ukrainiens
evidence.claim: The federal government decided that from 1 June 2022 Ukrainian refugees could access basic social-security benefits, healthcare coverage, integration courses, and job-center support, with Germany4Ukraine as a central information portal.
evidence.locator: Archival article dated 27 April 2022; sections 'Aides provenant d'une source unique' and support details
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous government decision and implementation summary with concrete benefits and dates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level attribution under Scholz; this is executive policy in the target year.
contrary_evidence: This is protection and integration policy, not direct evidence on policing or political violence.
The policy concerns refugees from Ukraine, so it is a targeted vulnerable-group measure rather than a universal domestic-safety fix.

evidence.title: Ergebnisse - Die Bundeswahlleiterin
evidence.claim: The 2021 Bundestag election was formally certified, with SPD at 25.7 percent of second votes and the new Bundestag at 736 seats; the page also notes the archived final result for the 26 September 2021 election.
evidence.locator: section 'Ergebnisse bei der Hauptwahl vom 26. September 2021' and results table
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary electoral authority source with certified result data.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline immediately before the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Baseline context, not direct Scholz conduct; it establishes the competitive election that brought him to office.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2021 baseline, not 2022 conduct.
It shows the system, not any ruler-specific democratic reform.

reasons.reason: This is inherited baseline from 2021, not 2022 Scholz conduct; it should stay as context only.

evidence.title: Einsprüche anlässlich der Wahl zum 20. Deutschen Bundestag
evidence.claim: The Bundestag voted on the Wahlprüfungsausschuss recommendation for election objections concerning the 2021 federal election; the page explains that election review is a Bundestag matter and that any eligible voter can file an objection and later appeal to the Constitutional Court.
evidence.locator: section 'Der Wahlprüfungsausschuss' and the vote result block
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary parliamentary record of lawful post-election review and legislative processing.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to electoral contestability.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional rather than personal; it reflects the democratic review architecture under Scholz's chancellorship.
contrary_evidence: This is review after the prior election, not evidence of a 2022 contested election campaign.
The decision path runs through parliament rather than the executive.

reasons.reason: Electoral review procedure is institutional context, not direct ruler action.

evidence.title: Urteil vom 22. März 2022
evidence.claim: The Court said the Basic Law does not create specific opposition-franchise rights, but it recognizes effective opposition as a constitutional principle and held the applicant was not obviously violated by the election of Bundestag vice presidents.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative constitutional ruling on parliamentary opposition rights and free mandate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; it shows judicially enforced democratic constraints during Scholz's term.
contrary_evidence: The court also declined to invent stronger opposition-specific rights.
It confirms that some opposition grievances can fail within a still-democratic framework.

reasons.reason: Constitutional-court protection of opposition norms is evidence of the legal environment, not a Scholz-initiated democratic reform.

evidence.title: Gericht lehnt AfD-Eilantrag zur Ausschussvorsitzendenwahl ab
evidence.claim: The Bundestag reported that the Constitutional Court rejected the AfD's request to install its committee-chair nominees and explained that the committees had used a free majority vote to choose their chairs.
evidence.locator: opening summary and section 'AfD-Kandidaten nicht zu Ausschussvorsitzenden gewählt'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary report on a contemporaneous court decision affecting opposition office access.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 check on parliamentary competition and minority rights.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional rather than Scholz-personal; it reflects parliamentary autonomy under his government.
contrary_evidence: The majority could deny opposition nominees those posts.
That is a democratic contest mechanism, not evidence of entrenchment.

evidence.title: Versammlungsrechtlicher Schutz eines Protestcamps und seiner infrastrukturellen Einrichtungen
evidence.claim: The Federal Administrative Court held that a protest camp can generally be protected as an assembly under Article 8 of the Basic Law and that necessary infrastructure can also fall under assembly protection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary domestic judicial ruling on assembly and protest protection.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 rule-of-law evidence on protest space.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; the ruling reflects the legal environment during Scholz's chancellorship.
contrary_evidence: Authorities can still impose limits in some circumstances.
The decision concerns protest rights generally, not Scholz's personal behavior.

evidence.title: Beschluss vom 30. März 2022
evidence.claim: The Court reiterated that press and broadcasting freedom protect the whole journalistic process, including access to needed information and sources, and that the state may not impose indirect pressures that amount to interference.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative constitutional decision on media freedom and access to information.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 legal context for media freedom.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; it establishes the constitutional framework under Scholz's government.
contrary_evidence: This does not show a specific Scholz initiative.
It is a general rights ruling rather than a case about media policy.

evidence.title: Erfolgreiche Verfassungsbeschwerde gegen die Übermittlung mit nachrichtendienstlichen Mitteln erhobener personenbezogener Daten
evidence.claim: The Court held that statutory rules requiring the transmission of personal data obtained by intelligence methods violated constitutional requirements of legal clarity and proportionality.
evidence.locator: press release body and opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional review of surveillance-data transfer limits.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional, not personal; it shows judicial limits on surveillance under Scholz.
contrary_evidence: This is a legal limit, not an executive anti-surveillance initiative.
It does not demonstrate whether the government changed practice immediately.

evidence.title: Unterlassene Auskunft der Bundesregierung zur Zahl der im Ausland tätigen Verfassungsschutzbediensteten verletzt parlamentarisches Fragerecht
evidence.claim: The Court ruled that the federal government's refusal to disclose the number of foreign-deployed constitutional-protection employees violated an MP's parliamentary question right.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ruling on parliamentary oversight and executive disclosure duties.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional rather than personal; it reflects the strength of parliamentary oversight during Scholz's term.
contrary_evidence: The case concerns disclosure, not direct policy substance.
It shows a check on the executive, not an affirmative freedom-expansion program.

evidence.title: Bundeskabinett - Ergebnisse

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous official cabinet decision with clear policy content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level action under Scholz; it reflects government policy rather than a personal order.
contrary_evidence: It is a draft-law step, not proof of downstream effects.
The proposal is preventive and indirect rather than a direct rights guarantee.

evidence.title: Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz bei der Chanukka-Feierstunde in der Heinz-Galinski-Schule am 19. Dezember 2022 in Berlin
evidence.claim: Scholz used the Chanukka speech to reaffirm Germany's historical responsibility toward Jewish life and remembrance, linking the fight against antisemitism to the protection of Jewish life in Germany.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Scholz speech in the federal bulletin archive.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 public stance on minority equality and protection.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz rhetoric; this is public stance rather than operational policy.
contrary_evidence: Symbolic speech is not the same as enforcement or institutional reform.
It does not by itself show how anti-antisemitism policy was implemented.

evidence.title: New Federal Government in office
evidence.claim: Olaf Scholz was elected Federal Chancellor with 395 votes and the new federal ministers were appointed and sworn in the same day.
evidence.locator: archive article body and photo captions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary federal-government record of the 2021 government transition.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline immediately before the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Baseline context for Scholz's 2022 authority, not a 2022 economic policy act itself.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2021 transition record, not an outcome measure for 2022.
It establishes office and appointment authority rather than economic competence.

evidence.title: Closed Cabinet meeting at Schloss Meseberg
evidence.claim: Scholz said the cabinet discussed energy security and energy supply with Economic Affairs Minister Robert Habeck and Finance Minister Christian Lindner in a constructive atmosphere.
evidence.locator: concluding press conference caption and quoted summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct federal-government archive with named participants and contemporaneous summary.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 cabinet coordination on the core economic shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz cabinet leadership; this shows he empowered the key economic ministers.
contrary_evidence: Constructive coordination is not the same as proven policy success.
It is an elite-level meeting, not evidence of household-level impact.

evidence.title: Der Mindestlohn steigt auf 12 Euro
evidence.claim: The Bundestag approved the government bill to raise the statutory minimum wage to 12 euro per hour from 1 October 2022, benefiting more than six million people, especially women and workers in eastern Germany.
evidence.locator: press release body and opening paragraph
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry announcement of an enacted policy with direct distributional effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level policy under Scholz; implementation was through the federal government and coalition majority.
contrary_evidence: A higher minimum wage can add some wage-cost pressure.
This is a targeted welfare measure, not a broad productivity reform by itself.

evidence.title: Mehr Unterstützung für Familien mit wenig Geld
evidence.claim: The cabinet approved a child immediate supplement of 20 euro per month and a one-off payment for people on social-security benefits as an early crisis response.

evidence.claim: The third relief package followed the first two packages of about 30 billion euro, adding further support for households and firms while explicitly aiming to preserve savings incentives amid the energy crisis.

Broader support can dilute targeting.

The package is crisis stabilization, not proof of long-run structural prosperity.

evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Germany 2023

evidence.title: Germany: 2023 Article IV Consultation - Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Germany
evidence.claim: The IMF said Germany’s policy response to spillovers from Russia’s war in Ukraine was timely and generally well designed, and it recommended fiscal tightening to support disinflation.

evidence.title: Gross domestic product up 1.9% in 2022

evidence.title: Nach Revision: Reallöhne im Jahr 2022 um 4,0 % gegenüber 2021 gesunken

evidence.title: Scholz vor Cum-Ex-Ausschuss: "Habe keinen Einfluss genommen"

evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly concerns the Chancellery's legal position under Scholz, but the ruling is about disclosure scope rather than truthfulness itself.
contrary_evidence: The ruling limited disclosure obligations; it did not resolve the underlying truthfulness allegation.

evidence.title: Alle Fraktionen für Transparenz und Aufklärung bei Cum-Ex

evidence.title: Neues Buch zur "Cum Ex"-Affäre: Protokolle nähren Zweifel an Erinnerungslücken von Scholz
evidence.claim: A new book and the released committee protocols renewed doubts about Scholz's claimed memory lapses, because they suggested he had given more concrete recollections in earlier Bundestag testimony than he later acknowledged.

**Office, Authority, Constraints**
Olaf Scholz was the ninth Federal Chancellor, elected on 8 December 2021, and in 2022 he led the first federal traffic-light coalition of SPD, Greens, and FDP. His office had real steering power under Article 65 of the Basic Law, but he was still constrained by Bundestag majority math, coalition bargaining, ministerial autonomy, and the fact that removal requires a constructive vote of no confidence.

**Compact Event Map**
- 8 Dec 2021: Scholz takes office with a three-party coalition and a reform-heavy coalition agreement.
- 24-27 Feb 2022: Russia invades Ukraine; Scholz answers with the Zeitenwende speech, sanctions, arms support, and the 100-billion-euro Bundeswehr fund.

- Summer 2022: the energy shock, inflation pressure, and coalition tradeoffs dominate domestic politics.
- 29 Sep 2022: the government unveils the 200-billion-euro economic shield and gas-price brake.
- Nov 2022: criticism sharpens over slow defense procurement and whether the Zeitenwende is moving fast enough.
